lines.text: Line one hundred eleven, with tolerance, changes the finish tolerances.
Line one hundred twenty-one, with end speed, makes a waypoint by hand: you pick the speed and switch radius.
Line one hundred thirty-one, passing through, is the easy way: give it the next point, and the corner rule picks both.
Each returns this, the same command, so they chain. The Drive Then Align auto does exactly that.
Line one hundred thirty-seven, goal, just asks the supplier. It's protected, so a subclass can replace it.
Drive To Tag replaces it: the goal measured from the tag, or else the map goal.
Drive To Piece: a spot forty centimeters short of the piece, facing it. No piece? Stay put.
That one method lets a moving goal use the same speed rule.
